text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "Verified against the code: notifications/sms.py imports get_household from registry.register and defines queue_sms exactly as R8 describes (sms_enabled guard, sms_ok guard, render, outbox append, returns SmsMessage). registry/register.py has load_households(*, active_only=False) which filters h.status == 'active' (line 13), so extending the import to bring in load_households is correct. Household has .site, .phone, .sms_ok and status 'active'|'inactive'|'merged' (core/models.py). TEMPLATES['DELIVERY_MOVED'] uses {site} and {day}, matching the params {'site': hh.site, 'day': day}. Iterating active households, filtering hh.site in sites and hh.sms_ok True, calling queue_sms(hh.id, 'DELIVERY_MOVED', ...) and returning the collected SmsMessage objects gives exactly one text per affected, opted-in household and reuses the existing guards and outbox, satisfying the notification part of LIFE-178."}}
reasoning:
The plan step: extend import from registry.register to also import load_households (the household-listing function supporting active_only). Check: registry/register.py has load_households(*, active_only=False) filtering h.status == "active" — matches R10. sms.py imports get_household from registry.register — matches. queue_sms exists as described, template DELIVERY_MOVED with {site} and {day} — matches. Household has .sms_ok, .site, .phone — matches.

The plan: iterate active households, keep hh.site in sites and hh.sms_ok True, call queue_sms(hh.id, 'DELIVERY_MOVED', {'site': hh.site, 'day': day}), collect and return SmsMessage objects. That satisfies "one text to each active household that collects at one of those sites and has agreed to receive texts, using the approved message with site and new day. Returns messages sent."

One subtlety: queue_sms raises RuntimeError if sms feature disabled — but that's existing behavior; the plan reuses it. Fine.

Everything checks out. Accept.
